label: Walt, 70, on warfarin, hit his head
message: This is Walt. I'm 70 and I take warfarin for my heart rhythm. Yesterday I hit my head on the kitchen cupboard door, pretty hard. There's a bump and a bit of a headache today but it's probably nothing. I didn't pass out. Just thought I'd mention it while I'm here.

early.patient_message: Go to the nearest emergency department now. A Counsel physician has been notified.

red_flags.excerpt: I hit my head on the kitchen cupboard door, pretty hard

questions: Have you had any vomiting, confusion, drowsiness, or vision changes since the injury?

result.justification: Relied on red flag anticoagulated_head_injury plus modifiers age_65_plus and anticoagulation; floor is ed_now. A 70-year-old on warfarin with a forceful head strike and a new headache the next day is at risk of delayed intracranial hemorrhage, which can occur even without loss of consciousness and with a minor-seeming injury. This needs prompt head CT and INR check, which cannot be done by phone or in a routine clinic visit. Not one level higher (call_911) because he is awake, communicating, did not lose consciousness, and reports no confusion, repeated vomiting, weakness or worsening symptoms, so he can be driven to the ED rather than needing an ambulance. Not lower (in_person_today or physician contact) because those levels cannot provide immediate CT imaging and would go below the floor.
result.safety_net: Go to the ED now and have someone else drive you; do not drive yourself. Do not take aspirin or ibuprofen. Call 911 immediately if you become drowsy or hard to wake, confused, have a worsening or severe headache, repeated vomiting, a seizure, fainting, weakness or numbness, trouble speaking, vision changes, unequal pupils, or clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears, or if the bump rapidly swells.
